name: Combined trend and carry portfolio

origin.source_title: Carry (NBER WP 19325, 2013; Journal of Financial Economics 2018)

how_it_works.simple: Run two simple ideas side by side: follow price trends, and own things that pay you to hold them. They tend to lose at different times, so together they are smoother.
how_it_works.analogy: Like owning both an umbrella shop and an ice cream stand: one of them usually has a good day.
how_it_works.precise: Allocate between a diversified time-series momentum strategy and a global carry factor (long high-carry, short low-carry within equities, bonds, currencies and commodities). Koijen et al. find carry strategies have little time-series momentum exposure, so the two returns have low correlation and the mix has a higher Sharpe ratio than either alone.

rule: Each month, run a 12-month time-series momentum book and a cross-sectional carry book in each asset class (each scaled to equal ex ante volatility); hold them in equal risk (or simple 50/50 weights) and rebalance monthly.
data_needed: Futures and forward prices across asset classes
Interest rates and futures curves to compute carry
Or the free AQR TSMOM and Century of Factor Premia datasets
economic_rationale: Carry earns a risk premium and trend earns a behavioral premium; Koijen et al. (2018) show carry returns are largely unrelated to time-series momentum, so combining them diversifies.
why_it_might_fail: Both legs weakened after publication: in AQR's data the All Macro carry factor had a Sharpe ratio of about -0.13 from 2013 to early 2026, and the 50/50 combination about 0.33 (catalog computation).

reported_results.source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt, Carry (NBER WP 19325), Table II, global carry factor
reported_results.market: Equities, bonds, currencies, commodities, credit, options
reported_results.notes: Carry legs weighted by inverse full-sample volatility (hindsight in weights). Passive equal-weight exposure to the same assets: Sharpe 0.47.

reported_results.source: Our calculation from Catalog computation: 50/50 AQR TSMOM and AQR All Macro Carry
reported_results.notes: Computed by the catalog on 2026-10-20 from the data file at source_url; this exact figure is not printed by the source. Arithmetic mean of monthly returns times 12; volatility is monthly standard deviation times sqrt(12); Sharpe uses excess returns; max drawdown from monthly compounding. Equal dollar weights on the two factor return series; TSMOM from https://www.aqr.com/-/media/AQR/Documents/Insights/Data-Sets/Time-Series-Momentum-Factors-Monthly.xlsx. Correlation between the legs 0.10. Same window: TSMOM alone Sharpe 0.97, carry alone 0.55. TSMOM dominates the risk because its volatility (12.5%) is far above carry's (3.7%).

Arithmetic mean of monthly returns times 12; volatility is monthly standard deviation times sqrt(12); Sharpe uses excess returns; max drawdown from monthly compounding. After the Carry working paper.

post_publication_evidence: In the catalog's computation from AQR data, the All Macro carry factor earned a Sharpe ratio of about 0.61 up to 2012 and about -0.13 from 2013 to early 2026, and currency carry fell from about 0.50 to 0.18. McLean and Pontiff (2016) find that across 97 published stock return predictors, portfolio returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication (https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.12365).

implementations.notes: Futures trading framework by Rob Carver; the provided rules folder includes ewmac.py (trend) and carry.py. Repo moved from robcarver17/pysystemtrade.

relevance.reason: FX carry plus FX trend is the most common systematic currency recipe, so this is the most direct multi-asset template and comparison for parity.
